explanation: Matches erdosproblems.com/1108: for every k ≥ 2, the set A of finite sums of distinct factorials n! (n ≥ 1) contains only finitely many k-th powers. Restricting the indices to n ≥ 1 agrees with the site's convention ℕ = {1,2,…}. If 0 were allowed, A would also contain 2 + Σ_{n≥2} n!, a slightly different set. The open question is stated affirmatively.
